mainTopic: End of מסכת שבת: the story of the cracked roof over a טומאת מת, the rule that one may seal, measure and tie on שבת, and עולא's challenge to רבה בר רב הונא about measuring that is not for a מצוה.
overview: This amud finishes the last משנה of מסכת שבת, a story about a cracked roof over a case of טומאת מת. To keep the טומאה from spreading on שבת, the people sealed a window with a clay vessel. They also tied a clay shard to a reed to check whether the crack in the roof was a full טפח. From what they did, the משנה learns that on שבת one may seal, measure and tie. The גמרא then tells a story. עולא saw רבה בר רב הונא measuring in a tub of water. עולא challenged him: the רבנן allowed measuring only when it is for a מצוה. רבה בר רב הונא answered that he was only a מתעסק, acting with no intent to measure, so it does not count as measuring. The amud ends with the הדרן for פרק מי שהחשיך, and with it all of מסכת שבת is complete.

steps.title: Sealing the window and measuring the crack in the roof
steps.stepSummary: The story ends: a cracked roof lay over the houses. The people sealed the window with a clay vessel and tied a shard to a reed to check whether the crack was a full טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a cracked roof lying on top of them. They sealed the window with a clay vessel. They tied a clay shard to a reed to find out whether the roof had an opening of one טפח or not.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a story about a case of טומאת מת. The people did three things on שבת to keep the טומאה from spreading: they sealed the window, they tied a shard to a reed, and they measured the opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the opening in the roof is one טפח or more, the roof does not count as a full אהל over the whole area, so the טומאה does not spread under all of it. That is why the exact size of the crack mattered. Sealing the window kept the טומאה out of the house, and the shard on a reed let them measure the opening.

keyTerms.meaning: A cracked roofing or covering (a cracked tub-like cover)

steps.whyThisMatters: These three actions (sealing, tying, measuring) become the source for the rule stated in the next step.

phrases.english: and a cracked roofing was placed on top of them.
phrases.notes: The roof over the two houses and the alley.

phrases.english: And they sealed the window with an earthenware vessel,
phrases.notes: So the impurity would not enter the house.

phrases.english: and they tied the earthenware shard with reed-grass
phrases.notes: This is a tying action done on שבת.

phrases.english: to know whether there is there, in the roofing,
an opening of a handbreadth or not.
phrases.notes: This is a measuring action done on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the story, they sealed, tied and measured on שבת to deal with טומאת מת.

steps.title: The lesson: sealing, measuring and tying are allowed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: From what these people did, we learn that on שבת one may seal an opening, measure, and tie.
steps.simpleTranslation: From their words we learned that one may seal, measure and tie on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The text draws the practical rule out of the story. Because these people did these actions on שבת, they must be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measuring is normally a weekday activity that the רבנן forbade on שבת. Here it was done to protect טהרה, which is a מצוה purpose, so it was allowed. The commentators (רש"י) explain that the tying was a קשר שאינו של קיימא, a knot not meant to last, which is not the forbidden kind of tying.

keyTerms.meaning: And from their words (actions) we learned

steps.whatToRemember: Sealing, measuring and tying are allowed on שבת in a case like this, where there is a מצוה need.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is what עולא will refer to in the next story.

phrases.english: And from their words we learned
that one may seal, and measure, and tie on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general rule out of the actions described in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may seal, measure and tie on שבת (in a מצוה context).

steps.title: עולא sees רבה בר רב הונא measuring in a tub
steps.stepSummary: עולא visited the house of the ריש גלותא. He saw רבה בר רב הונא sitting in a tub of water and measuring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא came to the house of the ריש גלותא. He saw רבה בר רב הונא sitting in a tub of water and measuring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next move. It describes someone doing an act of measuring on שבת that does not look connected to any מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This scene tests how far the rule from step 2 goes. Measuring was allowed for the טומאה case, but here there is no clear מצוה purpose. The story is preparing for עולא's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Babylonia

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to the house of the Exilarch.
He saw Rabba bar Rav Huna
who was sitting in a tub of water

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case that tests the rule about measuring from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבה בר רב הונא was measuring in water on שבת.

steps.title: עולא objects: measuring is allowed only for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: עולא challenges רבה בר רב הונא. The רבנן only allowed measuring that is for a מצוה, and this measuring is not for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The רבנן said you may measure when it is for a מצוה. Did they say you may measure when it is not for a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא attacks what רבה בר רב הונא is doing. He points out that the rule allowing measurement on שבת only applies when there is a מצוה need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא reads the rule from step 2 narrowly: it was said about measuring for טהרה, which is a מצוה. Measuring in a bathtub has no מצוה purpose, so in his view the רבנן's ban on weekday measuring should still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that the רבנן said (this applies only to...)
Was it said? (asked as a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 2 does not mean every kind of measuring is allowed on שבת. עולא is showing that the permission is limited to a מצוה need.

phrases.english: He said to him: Say that the Sages said it
about a measurement for a מצוה;
about one that is not for a מצוה, did they say it?
phrases.notes: A question that is really a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action described in step 3, based on the limits of the rule in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא measuring the water on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The permission to measure was only given for a מצוה. This measuring has no מצוה purpose, so it should be forbidden.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא answers: I am only acting without intent
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא answers that he is only a מתעסק. He is not actually trying to measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am just busying myself, with no real intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא defends himself. He says his act is not real measuring at all, because he has no interest in the measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with עולא's rule that measuring is allowed only for a מצוה. He agrees with it. His point is that what he is doing is not a measurement, because a מתעסק has no intention to measure, so the ban never applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone acting without intent toward the forbidden result

steps.whatToRemember: Measuring on שבת is forbidden unless it is for a מצוה. But an act done as a מתעסק, with no intent to measure, is not counted as measuring.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am merely acting unawares (without intent).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the act is not counted as measuring.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה בר רב הונא was doing a forbidden measurement that had no מצוה purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was a מתעסק with no intent to measure, so no forbidden measuring took place.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing מי שהחשיך and completing מסכת שבת
steps.stepSummary: The הדרן for פרק מי שהחשיך. With this, מסכת שבת is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק מי שהחשיך, and מסכת שבת is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing formula for the last פרק. It also marks the end of the whole מסכת שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is not part of the argument. It is a traditional sign-off that says the learner hopes to return to this material again.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Mi Shehechshich,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter and the tractate.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק מי שהחשיך and of מסכת שבת.
